cycle.label: Reporting period
cycle.note: Licenses expire June 30 every three years. CPE must be done by December 31 of the year before, over three calendar years.

requirements.label: Total CPE
requirements.note: Due by December 31 of the year before your license expires. Renew between January 1 and April 30; the license lapses July 1 if not renewed.
requirements.warning: Missed December 31? You can request a CPE extension and carry back hours completed by June 30 — only one extension in any six years, and carried-back hours can't count again toward your next period.

requirements.label: Non-technical
requirements.note: Maximum, not a target. No more than 60 non-technical hours (communication, management, leadership, client relations, practice development, motivational) count.

requirements.label: Washington Board-approved ethics
requirements.note: A 4-hour ethics and regulation course from a Washington Board-approved provider. Other ethics courses count toward the 120 but not this. We count courses with "Washington" and "ethics" in the title — edit the title if yours isn't picked up.

newLicensee.note: Your first period runs from your license issue date to December 31 of the year before your license expires — the full 120 hours, at least 20 in each calendar year (including the first, partial one).

licenseDateHint: Washington licenses expire June 30 every three years (e.g. 06/30/2028). CPE is due by December 31 of the year before.
issueDateHint: If your license was issued during this period, your first period starts on this date.
limitsNotTracked: Board service, first-time instruction/development and authorship: max 60 combined, and they don't count toward the 20-hour yearly minimum.
toVerify: Non-technical mapping (WAC 4-30-132 wasn't readable from here): Communications and Marketing, Personal Development, Personnel/HR, Business Management and Organization, Production and Behavioral Ethics treated as non-technical; Computer Software and Applications as technical.
Whether a Washington-approved ethics course also counts as technical (we count it toward the 120 and keep it out of the non-technical cap).
Carry-back hours (Jan 1 – June 30 of the renewal year, with an extension) are explained on the dashboard but not added to the numbers.
